title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: OCR scanning of images on Mac devices
summary: Hold: the briefing gives Teams the endpoint file-size limit, although Microsoft limits Teams images to 20 MB. Billing setup also requires owner or contributor rights to the Azure subscription, which the briefing omits.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans OCR support on Mac endpoints to detect sensitive content in images and apply Purview policies.
claims.quote: We are adding OCR support on Mac endpoints to detect sensitive content in images and apply policies to protect these images.

claims.claim: The roadmap description says images are not supported for content scanning on Mac endpoint devices today.
claims.quote: images are not supported for content scanning today on Mac endpoint devices.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can block, warn or audit copying protected files to USB media on macOS.
claims.quote: Copy to a USB removable media – When enforced, this action blocks, warns, or audits the copying or moving of protected files from an endpoint device to USB removable media.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can block, warn or audit copying protected files to network shares on macOS.
claims.quote: Copy to network shares – When enforced, this action blocks, warns, or audits the copying or moving of protected files from an endpoint device to any network share.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can block, warn or audit printing protected files on macOS.
claims.quote: Print – When enforced, this action blocks, warns, or audits when protected files are printed from an endpoint device.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can block, warn or audit copying protected-file data to the clipboard on macOS.
claims.quote: Copy to clipboard – When enforced, this action blocks, warns, or audits data in protected file that is being copied to a clipboard on an endpoint device.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can block, warn or audit protected-file uploads to cloud services on macOS.
claims.quote: Upload to cloud – This action blocks, warns, or audits when protected files are uploaded or prevented from being uploaded to cloud services based on the allow/unallowed domains list in global settings.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can prevent unallowed applications from accessing protected files on macOS.
claims.quote: Accessed by unallowed apps – When enforced, this action prevents applications that are on the unallowed apps list (as defined in Global settings) from accessing protected files on an endpoint device.
